title: Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) — Estate Retirement on Approval, Offset and Payment to the Estate
content:
# Estate Retirement on Approval, Offset and Payment to the Estate

**Board policy, Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).** These clauses govern an estate retirement once the estate's application has been approved, and an application that is denied or withdrawn.

## Retired clauses

The following two clauses are **no longer in force**. They have been superseded by the current basis and are carried here only so that the former wording is recognised as retired.

- *Retired:* "On approval every unretired allocation of every capital account of the deceased member is retired as special retirement entries of the estate type, up to the estate annual cap of gross retirement in the calendar year (the gross estate retirement of the calendar year across every capital account of the deceased member), oldest allocation years first." — no longer in force.
- *Retired:* "Where the class pays estate retirements at a discounted present value, each row's payable is its amount discounted at the estate discount rate for the number of whole years remaining until the year it would be retired in the general rotation (its allocation year plus the class's expected rotation years), never fewer than zero years." — no longer in force.

The class figures those clauses named (the estate discount rate, the expected rotation years and the estate annual cap) remain the figures of each patron class.

## Clauses in force

1. **Offset first.** The payable for the estate is offset first against the deceased member's unpaid final-billed balances, in the same way as every capital credit payout is offset — the positive balances of the deceased member's final-billed service accounts, oldest final balance first.
2. **One check to the estate.** The rest is paid by one check payable to the estate within the class's estate payment period — 30 calendar days after board approval in every class that offers estate retirement.
3. **Denial or withdrawal.** A denied or withdrawn application returns the account to inactive, and the credits return to the general rotation.
4. **Closing.** Once the board-approved estate retirement has been paid and nothing remains unretired or payable on the account, the account becomes fully retired.

## Hypothetical illustration

An estate is owed $640.00 after approval on a third-Tuesday board meeting, and the deceased member's records show one final-billed service account with an unpaid balance of $95.25. The offset takes $95.25 against that balance, and one check of $544.75 is issued to the estate no later than the 30th calendar day after the approval date.

| Event | Account status afterwards |
|---|---|
| Application denied | inactive |
| Application withdrawn by the claimant | inactive |
| Approved retirement paid, nothing left unretired or payable | fully retired |

superseded_clauses: On approval every unretired allocation of every capital account of the deceased member is retired as capital_special_retirement rows with retirement_type estate, up to estate_annual_cap of gross retirement in the calendar year (capital_msr_estate_retired_year), oldest allocation years first.

Where estate_discount_applies is true each row's payable is its amount discounted at estate_discount_rate_pct for the number of whole years remaining until the year it would be retired in the general rotation (its allocation_year plus estate_expected_rotation_years), never fewer than zero years.
